name: Act of June 5, 1872 confirming the Kaw (Kansa) reservation in Indian Territory
promises: Congress confirmed a reserve selected for the Kansa in Indian Territory, from the Arkansas River at the Kansas line down to the line between townships 26 and 27, then by section lines north to the Kansas line (Royce schedule).
Under the same Act the Osage were to permit the Kansa to settle within the Osage tract, the Kansa paying for the land (Royce schedule).

openQuestions: A reservation grant, bought by the Kansa from the Osage, not a cession. Royce area 535 is the Kaw reservation.
The ICC title search for "kaw" returned only Docket 33 (1950-1954), which concerns the Kansas lands ceded in 1825, not this reservation.
The allotment of the Kaw reservation and later federal acquisitions there were not researched.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for: Court of Claims names "kaw", "kansa"; ICC full text "Kaw reservation 1872", "Kaw Indian Territory" (Docket 33 only). Found Kansas or Kaw Tribe v. United States, 80 Ct. Cl. 264 (1934), which held the Kaw's interest under this Act limited to the tract set apart and paid for; a ruling against the Kaw, added to today. No breach finding.
today: In Kansas or Kaw Tribe v. United States (1934) the Court of Claims held that the Kaw bought, under this Act, only the 100,137.32 acres set apart and paid for out of their funds, as the Cherokee deed of June 14, 1883 recites, not an undivided share of the whole Osage reservation, and denied that claim; this went against the Kaw.
